title: Essential Knife Skills: Grip, Slice, Dice, Mince — with Lan Lam
summary: Lan Lam demonstrates core knife skills in a practical kitchen context, beginning with a story about brunoise to motivate precision and efficiency. He emphasizes a sharp chef’s knife, a pinch grip, and ergonomic alignment from shoulder to blade; he explains safe offhand positioning and fingertip protection. The lesson covers slicing (including diagonal push cuts and pull cuts), dicing (including decisions about edge squaring versus waste), and mincing (with a focus on delicate herbs). He also shows garlic technique to maximize flavor, and closes with a real-world application through Japchae, illustrating how these skills translate to efficient, less-wasteful cooking in the home kitchen. The video blends technique demonstrations with commentary on form, control, and safety, inviting viewer practice and engagement.

sections.title: Introduction and Brunoise concept
sections.description: Lan Lam opens with a personal anecdote about brunoise and emphasizes the value of sharpened knife skills for efficiency, accuracy, and waste reduction.

sections.title: Grip and ergonomics: pinch grip and alignment
sections.description: Describes the default pinch grip and the idea of the knife as an extension of the arm, including the ergonomic line from shoulder through the wrist to the blade tip.

sections.title: Board setup, offhand and fingertip safety
sections.description: Discusses keeping the board usable, avoiding awkward angles, and tucking fingertips to protect them and aid control.

sections.title: Slicing technique: diagonal push cut with back-half blade
sections.description: Explains using the back half of the blade in a diagonal, forward-and-down motion for efficiency, while the blade’s micro serrations and the knuckles guide precision.

sections.title: Pull cut for delicate foods
sections.description: Introduces an alternative pull-cut motion for delicate ingredients, offering a low-pressure slicing option.

sections.title: Dicing fundamentals and edge considerations
sections.description: Outlines the steps for dicing (slices → strips → cubes) and discusses tradeoffs between perfectly uniform dice and higher yield when edges are not squared.

sections.title: Onion-specific dicing method
sections.description: Details halved onions and the sequence of horizontal then vertical cuts, including rotating the onion to improve control and maintain a stable grip near the root.

sections.title: Mincing herbs: delicate, low-damage technique
sections.description: Defines mincing as a fine chop, then demonstrates a two-direction approach that minimizes vertical motion to preserve color and aroma.

sections.title: Garlic technique to maximize allicin release
sections.description: Shows smashing garlic to rupture cells and release allicin, including briefly switching grip to share workload between hands.

sections.title: Japchae as knife-skills showcase
sections.description: Uses japchae to illustrate how practiced knife skills translate to a real dish, highlighting efficiency and texture in vegetables.

sections.title: Wrap-up and audience engagement
sections.description: Concludes with reflections and a prompt for viewers to share their go-to knife and to engage with comments, likes, and further resources.
